description: The version 3 pool, in the pool-v2.json case shape (see its description), for a file that says formatVersion 3. Items and series also carry studios: the server's studio names as sent (before the studio fold; a matcher folds both sides, and the fold is idempotent, so a client that cleans the names when it reads them gets the same result). Sources and exclusions may use type studio; filters may hold tags, studios, notGenres and runtime (with the version 3 episode and movie windows). expected is the pool as the pool evaluator gives it, without the runtime part of filters, which is applied where the epoch's pool is cut (The pool of an epoch). A case whose filters hold runtime also gives each item runtimeMs (decimal string) and expectedAfterRuntime, the pool after the runtime part too, with every other epoch condition taken as passed. films is the version 2 film-to-collection map (collections named in sources). franchises, in every case, is the franchise map of curated: each movie of the pool that is a member movie of any collection of the snapshot, mapped to the smallest such collection ID (32 ASCII bytes, unsigned); an empty object when none. Strings are written with \u escapes for everything outside ASCII; one case has an unpaired surrogate escape in an item's studio name.

cases.name: studio source: a movie's own studio and an episode's series' studio match, ASCII letters fold
cases.note: ...0201 takes series ...0301's studio. ...0203 has the studio itself (its series has another). ...0204 is a loose episode with its own studio.

cases.name: studio source: the studio fold cleans both sides (no-break space trimmed, zero-width space and soft hyphen dropped, tab and line separator become a space)
cases.note: In: trailing U+00A0 trimmed; U+200B dropped; a leading tab becomes a space and is trimmed; U+2028 between the words becomes a space; U+00AD dropped; U+FEFF dropped and a trailing U+3000 trimmed; U+0085 (in U+007F to U+009F) dropped. ...0115 has a tab between the words (written as one space) and a trailing space (trimmed). Out: two spaces stay two; ö does not fold; U+200C is kept (not in the dropped set); a no-break space inside the name is not trimmed and is not a space; no space at all.

cases.name: studio source: the rules name is cleaned too; a name that is only spaces and dropped characters matches nothing
cases.note: The first source cleans to STUDIO A and folds to studio a. The second cleans to nothing: it matches nothing, not even the items whose studio also cleans to nothing (such a studio is dropped).

cases.name: studio source: an episode whose series is not in the snapshot uses its own studios (no fail closed)
studio source: a lone surrogate in a server studio name is dropped
cases.note: The item names hold an unpaired surrogate (JSON escape \ud800 or \udfff alone), which the clean step drops. The emoji (a valid pair) is kept, so ...0103 does not match. A rules name with an unpaired surrogate would make the file invalid, so only item names carry one.

cases.name: studio exclusion: removes a movie of the studio and every episode of a series of the studio; it does not fail closed
cases.note: Series ...0399 is not in the snapshot: ...0203 stays (a studio exclusion is not fail-closed, unlike a genre or tag exclusion); ...0204 is removed by its own studio.

cases.name: studio source and exclusion together, with a genre source: the exclusion wins
filters studios: any of the studios, under the studio fold; an episode takes its series' studios; a missing series uses its own only
cases.note: The filter's third name cleans to nothing and matches nothing; the second cleans to Studio B. ...0203's series is missing and it has no studio of its own: it fails, but the filter does not fail closed (...0202 passes on its own studio).

cases.name: filters tags: any of the names, ASCII letters fold only; an episode takes its series' tags; a missing series uses its own only
cases.note: Tags are matched as a tag source: a trailing space is not trimmed and non-ASCII letters do not fold.

cases.name: filters notGenres: none of the names; an episode also takes its series' genres; it fails closed on a missing series
cases.note: ...0201's series has Horror. ...0203 has it itself. ...0204 and ...0205 have series ...0399, which is not in the snapshot: they fail whatever their own genres are. ...0206 and ...0207 are loose episodes, checked on their own genres.

cases.name: filters notGenres with genres: an item needs one of genres and none of notGenres
cases.note: ...0203 passes genres on its own genre (that filter does not fail closed) but fails notGenres (it does).

cases.name: filters notGenres AND tags AND studios AND kind AND the rating ceiling
cases.note: ...0101 is a movie; ...0202's series is Horror; ...0203's series has no Pick tag; ...0204's series is Studio B; ...0205's series is over the ceiling.

cases.name: filters runtime: a general window and one for each kind, at their edges (expectedAfterRuntime)
cases.note: The runtime part is applied where the epoch's pool is cut, not by the pool evaluator, so expected leaves it out; expectedAfterRuntime is the pool after the runtime part too (runtimeMs as at the cut-off). Movie window 80 to 150 minutes: 4,799,999 ms out, 4,800,000 in, 9,000,000 in, 9,000,001 out. Episode window up to 30 minutes: 1,800,000 in, 1,800,001 out. ...0204 is out by the general window (181 min > 180) and its own window.

cases.name: filters runtime: only an episode window: films are not limited by it
cases.note: Episode window 2 to 181 minutes: ...0203 (60,000 ms) is out; ...0204 (181 min exactly) is in. Every movie stays, up to 1440 minutes.

cases.name: filters runtime: only a movie window with a minimum, and a general minimum
franchise map: every collection of the snapshot is a candidate, not only the named ones (the films map stays empty)
cases.note: No collection is a source, so the version 2 films map is empty; the franchise map of curated still groups the films.

cases.name: franchise map: a film in several collections maps to the smallest collection ID, named or not
cases.note: The films map (named collections only) gives ...04f2 to both films; the franchise map takes the smallest ID among all collections each film is in.

cases.name: franchise map: the smallest ID is by ASCII bytes (a digit before a letter)
franchise map: episodes are never mapped (member episodes, member series, member seasons); a collection of shows maps nothing
franchise map: only films of the pool are mapped (excluded, filtered out or over the ceiling: not in it)
franchise map: a collection that is only an exclusion or not in the snapshot maps nothing
cases.note: Collection ...04ff is a source but not in the snapshot: it selects and groups nothing. Collection ...0402 is an exclusion: it removes ...0102, so that film is not in the pool and not in the map.
